title: Wildfire Potential — Hourly Forecast, United States (RRFS)
abstract:
Where conditions favour wildfire growth over the next three and a half days.

This is a forecast of fire potential, not of fire itself. It combines the near-surface weather that drives fire behaviour — wind, temperature, humidity — with the state of the fuels on the ground, into a single hourly index. Bright areas are where a fire, if one starts or is already burning, would find conditions to grow and spread. Dark, clear areas are where conditions are unfavourable.

The index is unitless: higher means more favourable to fire. It says nothing about whether a fire exists, only about what the weather and fuels would do if one did. Read it alongside the smoke forecasts to see the difference between where fire could spread and where smoke has actually gone.

An 84-hour hourly outlook on the NOAA Rapid Refresh Forecast System's 3 km CONUS domain, each frame an hourly average rather than an instant. Frames are data-encoded: the brightness of each pixel carries the measured value, so hovering reports the index rather than a colour.
